title: Chevron Applies for RIGI Investment Incentive for $13.8B Vaca Muerta Unconventional Oil Project
detail: Chevron Corporation applied for admission to Argentina's RIGI (Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones) investment incentive program for a $13.8 billion unconventional oil development project in the Vaca Muerta shale formation. The application — one of the largest single RIGI applications since the regime was enacted under Milei's government — targets large-scale unconventional oil production expansion in Neuquén Province. Under RIGI, qualifying projects receive a 15% corporate tax rate (vs. standard 25%), zero export tariffs, and accelerated depreciation. Chevron is already one of Vaca Muerta's largest operators through its partnership with YPF, and this new application signals a major scaling of that commitment. The news reinforced Argentina's profile as a top-tier Latin American energy investment destination amid high global oil prices.
